Operator
Good afternoon, and welcome to Siemens Energy's Pre-Close Group Call for the Q2 of fiscal year 2026. Before we begin, please note that today's call is being recorded. The recording will be available on Siemens Energy's website until the quarterly results are published on 12 May 2026. Before we begin, I would like to draw your attention to the information and forward-looking statements notice, which you have agreed to by signing up to this call, which applies to comments made during the call today. At this time, I would like to turn the call over to your host today, Mr. Tobias Hang. Please go ahead, sir.
Tobias Hang
Head of Investor Relations, Siemens Energy
Thank you so much, Moritz. Good afternoon, good evening, and a warm welcome to the Siemens Energy Q2 fiscal year 2026 pre-close call. The purpose of today's call is to reinforce our previously communicated guidance and to recap key information already shared at quarterly results calls, conferences, and roadshows. We plan to publish our Q2 fiscal year 2026 results at 7:00AM CEST on Tuesday, 12 May 2026, with the webcast scheduled for 10:30AM CEST the same day.
Our silent period will begin immediately after this call on 31 March 2026. As always, we will share the company-compiled consensus one week ahead of the earnings release on Tuesday, 5 May 2026, after market close. Let me briefly guide you through today's agenda. I will begin with our assessment of the current situation in the Middle East.
I will then share our perspective on market developments, demand, and pricing trends before touching on seasonality and concluding with a few additional updates for Q2. As our disclosure is restricted to the information already covered during the call, we will conclude today's session without a Q&A. Thank you for your understanding. Starting now with the current situation in the Middle East. For us, one priority stands above all else at this time, the safety of approximately 3,000 employees in the region.
At the same time, we are doing everything we can to ensure continuity for our customers and partners to support the reliable operation of energy systems. In fiscal year 2025, the Middle East accounted for a high single-digit percentage of group backlog and revenue. Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar are the core countries, with Saudi Arabia by far the largest.
It's also important to keep in mind that we do not meaningfully export from this region into other regions. While we do not have major supply chain dependencies on the Middle East, we're continuously monitoring the situation for potential consequential effects. From business perspectives, while we see impacts on local projects, we do not see a material direct impact on our guidance at the current point in time.
The primary impact from the conflict is on logistics and shipping, not the underlying demand, which can lead to project-level delays and shifts in revenue recognition and cash timing. Potential indirect effects, such as severe logistical constraints in the event of a prolonged or high-intensity conflict or a deterioration in investment sentiments, are currently not assumed, but are being closely monitored. With regard to longer-term impacts, it is too early to draw a conclusion at this stage.
Let us continue how we see the market more broadly. The market context remains the same as we laid out at the Capital Market Day and reiterated in the Q1 calls. We operate in a structurally growing electricity market rather than a short-term cyclical environment. Expect an elevated gas turbine market at least until 2035. On the grid side, we see a once-in-a-generation investment cycle over the next 15 years, driven by the need to connect renewables and replace aging assets. By 2040, around half of installed transformers will have reached retirement age. These themes underpin the demand strengths we are seeing across our portfolio. Demand is real and accelerating, and the key challenge is capacity and speed rather than appetite. Turning now to demand and pricing in Gas Services.
The Q1 order intake of 13GW was exceptionally strong, with demand broad-based across regions, customers, and applications. That said, quarterly order intake will remain volatile, reflecting the large multi-year project nature of the business. We expect another strong Q2, followed by a weaker H2 of fiscal year 2026, reflecting the timing embedded in slot reservation agreements rather than any indication of a weakening market environment.
With respect to gas turbine capacity, we are sold out until fiscal year 2028, with fiscal year 2029 slots filling up very quickly and in high demand. We have also started seeing some slots for fiscal year 2030 being booked. As we approach the end of the year, we do expect fiscal year 2029 to be largely sold out, with limited capacity available fiscal year 2030.
When it comes to signing orders beyond that timeframe, we will need to ensure that the broader supply chain and our EPC partners have demonstrated sufficient execution capacity. Supply chain blades and vanes remain the industry's principal bottleneck and our number one limiting factor. In Q1, we confirmed that pricing momentum remains favorable with further new units year-over-year margin uplift, and we expect this trend to continue in the foreseeable future.
We have also confirmed that current slot reservation agreements are signed with higher pricing versus current orders. When it comes to service, the starting point in terms of service profitability is already very strong, but better pricing for new service contracts in our order backlog continues. Nevertheless, we need to be mindful that it takes time on the better-priced service contract starts to convert through the P&L.
To elaborate, new turbines first need to be shipped and installed. Minor inspections typically begin two to three years thereafter, and major outages usually start roughly five years later. As a result, the real margin uplift from services will become much more visible towards the end of this decade or the beginning of the next, clearly beyond fiscal year 2028. Overall, demand for gas turbines and services remains structurally strong.
The market is tight, pricing momentum remains favorable, and while order intake will remain volatile, the full benefit of attractive service margins will materialize gradually over time. Let me continue with demand and pricing in Grid Technologies. The market has doubled over the last three years, and we continue to see further growth across all regions. Our book-to-bill in Grid Technologies has been at or above two for three consecutive years.
Globally, customers are accelerating investments in transmission capacity to integrate renewables, meet rising demands, and strengthen stability. The challenge is delivery time rather than demand. Even with factory expansions on the way, transmission demand continues to outpace industry capacity. In Q1, we confirmed that pricing has plateaued at high levels in Europe. The message we have been consistent on for five quarters now. In the US, pricing is still moving up for certain products, particularly where customers value short, shorter lead times.
Looking ahead, further margin improvement in Grid will be driven primarily by productivity and operational excellence. Across both new and existing facilities, we are investing heavily in automation, including robotics and AI, as well as further digitalization and simplification of production processes. Let me now turn to Siemens Gamesa. The offshore wind market has recently seen attractive auction outcomes, such as the UK's Round 7.
In addition, the targets agreed at the North Sea Summit reinforce our confidence that offshore wind will remain an attractive market in selected regions globally. We were also pleased to secure the first orders in our SG 7.0 platform, the successor of the 5.X in Q1. This provides tangible evidence that our turnaround strategy is translating into market traction. For Siemens Gamesa, the trajectory outlined in Q1 remains unchanged. We expect H1 to be negative and H2 to be positive, with full year breakeven remaining the clear commitment.
Our capital allocation framework remains unchanged. We have committed to up to EUR 6 billion of share buyback through fiscal year 2028. The first tranche, with a maximum volume of EUR 2 billion, started on 4 March. Progress on the share buyback is published weekly on our investor relations website.
Just as today, we just published the latest results. Now let's briefly discuss seasonality across our business areas. In Gas Services, order intake for fiscal year 2026 is expected to be above fiscal year 2025, with a stronger H1. As mentioned earlier, we caution against annualizing the exceptionally strong Q1 order intake. It is also important to remember that strong order intake is typically paired with down payments, which support free cash flow, as we saw in fiscal year 2025.
In terms of profitability in Gas Services, the historical pattern remains unchanged. Profitability is typically stronger in the H1 of the year, reflecting the service season and the new unit to service mix. This will still be the case in fiscal year 2026, although the effect will be less pronounced as better margin new unit business begins to convert through the P&L.
For Grid Technologies, order intake in fiscal year 2026 should be at or slightly above fiscal year 2025, reflecting the strong market environment shown at the Capital Market Day. However, due to the lumpiness of large HVDC orders and projects, individual quarters may deviate from the average. Underlying profit margin in Grid are expected to be relatively stable across the quarters, with limited seasonality in line with previous years.
Please remember that the last year's Q2 profitability was elevated by a positive one-off item of around EUR 100 million. For Transformation of Industry, quarterly profit margins are expected to be relatively stable across the year. Again, in line with historical patterns. For Siemens Gamesa, as mentioned earlier, we expect a negative H1, a positive H2, and full year breakeven.
Finally, due to the timing shift of some offshore auctions, offshore order intake in fiscal year 2026 is expected to be relatively muted, with some projects shifting into the next fiscal year. CapEx for fiscal year 2026 remains around EUR 2.5 billion. Given that we spent only EUR 347 million in Q1, CapEx will increase significantly over the remaining three quarters. Additional Q2 updates, which finally we will provide a brief comment on the foreign exchange.
As we guide on comparable revenue growth, excluding currency translation and portfolio effects, we continue to see materially higher comparable growth than nominal growth. This is mainly driven by US dollar to euro volatility, specifically the devaluation of the US dollar.
As a result, for the Q2, we expect comparable revenue growth to be around 600 basis points higher than nominal growth at group level, compared with 460 basis points in Q1. With that, we will conclude today's call. Thank you very much for your participation, and for continued engagement. As a final reminder, our results will be published at 7:00AM CEST on Tuesday, 12 May, with a webcast at 10:30AM CEST, and our silent period begins tomorrow on 31 March. With Easter approaching, we wish you a relaxing Easter break. Thank you and bye-bye.
Operator
Ladies and gentlemen, the conference is now concluded and you may disconnect. Thank you for joining, and have a pleasant day. Goodbye.

content.text:
Operator
Good morning. My name is Joanna, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to Energizer's fourth quarter and fiscal year 2025 conference call. After the speaker's remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star one on your touch-tone phone. As a reminder, this call is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Jonathan Poldan, Vice President, Treasurer, and Investor Relations. You may begin your conference.
Jonathan Poldan
Vice President of Investor Relations and Treasurer, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Good morning and welcome to Energizer's fourth quarter and fiscal 2025 conference call. Joining me today are Mark LaVigne, President and Chief Executive Officer, and John Drabik, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. In just a moment, Mark will share a few opening comments, and then we'll take your questions. A replay of this call will be available on the Investor Relations section of our website, energizerholdings.com. In addition, please note that our earnings release, prepared remarks, and a slide deck are also posted on our website. During the call, we will make forward-looking statements about the company's future business and financial performance, among other matters. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties, which may cause actual results to differ materially from these statements. We do not undertake to update these forward-looking statements.
Other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements are included in reports we file with the ESC. We also refer in our presentation to non-GAAP financial measures. The reconciliation of non-GAAP financial measures to comparable GAAP measures is shown in our press release issued earlier today, which is available on our website. Information concerning our categories and estimated market share discussed in this call relates to the categories where we compete, and is based on Energizer's internal data, data from industry analysis, and estimates we believe to be reasonable. The battery category information includes both brick-and-mortar and e-commerce retail sales. Unless otherwise noted, all comments regarding the quarter and year pertain to Energizer's fiscal year, and all comparisons to prior year relate to the same period in fiscal 2024. With that, I would like to turn the call over to Mark.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Good morning, and thanks for joining us today. We delivered strong earnings in fiscal 2025 by staying agile and focused in the face of a disruptive environment and shifting trade policies. We moved quickly, capitalized on opportunities, and executed with discipline to achieve outstanding results. Our decisive actions to reshape our operational footprint, combined with strategic investments and strong execution, have established an elevated earnings base, positioning Energizer to win as we close 2025 and move into 2026. Let me share a few highlights that define our progress in 2025. We grew net sales in a challenging environment, driven by significant growth in e-commerce, international expansion, and meaningful innovation in auto care. We made necessary changes to our network and executed targeted pricing to mitigate tariffs and preserve margins. Project Momentum achieved over $200 million in savings to date.
As we announced this morning, we have extended it into a fourth year focused on increased operational efficiency and the integration of Advanced Power Solutions. Our innovation pipeline is robust, designed to drive category growth and strengthen our leadership across batteries and auto care. Finally, through this transformation and strategic investments, we have established a stronger earnings foundation for the future. For the year, net sales grew 2.3% to nearly $3 billion. Adjusted earnings per share increased 6% to $3.52, supported by organic growth, disciplined cost management, and manufacturing production credits enabled by our investments in US production. We also returned $177 million to shareholders in fiscal 2025 through dividends and share repurchases, reducing our outstanding shares by roughly 5%. The macro environment continues to evolve. Tariffs have increased our costs, consumer demand softened late in the year, and supply chains required rapid rebalancing.
We responded quickly, realigning our manufacturing footprint to minimize tariff exposure and executing pricing actions to protect margins. These steps were not easy, but they were necessary and created a solid foundation for future growth. As we enter fiscal 2026, we know the first quarter will be transitional. It will reflect a challenging sales comparison, transitional tariff-related costs, and moderating consumer sentiment. Beyond Q1, the benefits of our actions, including network realignment, accelerated APS integration, and Project Momentum savings, will build. We expect these initiatives to drive double-digit adjusted earnings per share growth over the final three quarters of the year. In short, fiscal 2025 was a year of resilience, agility, and progress. We faced a challenging environment head-on, made bold decisions, and strengthened our foundation for the future. I want to thank our colleagues, suppliers, and customers for the collaboration that helped us overcome these headwinds and deliver.
This year-over-year growth reflects disciplined execution, and the strength of the partnerships built on trust and shared commitment to solving challenges together. Thank you for your continued confidence in Energizer. Together, we are ready to compete, win, and grow. With that, let's open the call for questions.
Operator
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer session. Should you have a question, please press the star followed by the one on your touch-tone phone. You will hear a prompt that your hand has been raised. If you wish to decline from the polling process, please press star followed by the two. If you are using a speakerphone, please flip the handset before pressing any keys. We do ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. You may certainly re-queue if you have additional questions. The first question comes from Peter Grom at UBS. Please go ahead.
Peter Grom
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Great. Thank you. Good morning, guys. Hope you're doing well. I wanted to pick up on that last point, just on the phasing into the year and specifically kind of the ramp needed to hit the full year following a challenging first quarter. Can you maybe just speak to the degree of confidence or maybe the visibility you have on the implied ramp, just given how difficult and dynamic the operating environment continues to be? Just related, I mean, what's the level of flexibility or cushion you've kind of embedded in the outlook at this stage? Thanks.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Thanks, Peter. Let me start. I'm going to hand it to John, and then I'll maybe finish in kind of how we approach providing outlook for the year. I mean, look, we acknowledge that we expected a stronger Q4, but I still think we want to take a step back, at least as we get started, and really reflect and be proud of what the organization achieved in 2025. To do that, I think you have to go back to when we launched Project Momentum three years ago. The objective behind that was to restore gross margins, enhance free cash flow, and strengthen the balance sheet. We have delivered across all of those metrics over that three-year period. We had $200 million in savings. We've recovered 350 basis points in gross margin, and Momentum has enhanced free cash flow or played a part in enhancing free cash flow.
We delivered more than $740 million in free cash flow over that time period. The result over that time period is nearly 5% EPS growth on average over that time period, and over 3% EBITDA growth. As we started momentum, we understood the need for supply chain agility. FY25 put that to an early test. With the tariff and trade policies, we needed to adjust fast, and we did. We overhauled our network. We preserved margins in '25, and this will get, Peter, to your question. We'll essentially do that in '26 once you incorporate kind of the APS margin integration that we're going to go through. There is a transitional period, which we saw in Q4. You're going to see in Q1, but the pieces are in place, and the plans are mostly complete for the ramp that John's going to describe.
It's really been a remarkable transformation, and as you said, in a really disruptive, volatile environment over the last three years, which ended in a sort of six-month sprint where we needed to rebalance our network to make sure that we took into account new trade policies. As we exit that sprint at the end of Q1, we're really set up from Q2, Q3, and Q4 to get back to more historical levels of performance from a financial perspective. Jon, you want to talk through the ramp?
Jonathan Poldan
Vice President of Investor Relations and Treasurer, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Yeah. Yeah. Let me start with the first quarter, and then we can kind of go into what we see in Q2 through Q4. On the top line in the first quarter, we've got both that storm comp and the shift in display timing that we called out. Both of those we view as one-time or timing in nature. As you look at the rest of it, the category overall, we're calling down for the quarter about 300 to 400 basis points, but we see that improving as we go throughout the quarter and then into the rest of the year. Our outlook for the full year on the category contemplates back to roughly flat in the back half.
We're going to lean into other areas for growth that have been driving us for the last year or two. That's really international markets, as well as transitioning that APS business into our Energizer branded portfolio. That's a big driver in the back half of our fiscal year. We're going to continue to see growth in e-com, and some of the innovation that we expect to launch this year. When you put those in place, I think we're going to get past the first quarter and start to see better growth in the back half of the year, really starting in Q2. Gross margins are also getting impacted in the first quarter.
As we get past the first quarter, we should benefit from getting past the transitional operational inefficiencies that we really generated over the summer and into the fall as we kind of moved our supply chain around to offset the tariffs. We'll further benefit from transitioning the APS business to our branded portfolio. I think that will help us on the margin side. As we look at Q2 through Q4, I think low single-digit top-line growth and normalized gross margins, with some of the momentum savings, should allow us to generate that EPS growth of kind of low double digits.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Peter, to wrap up on your final question, how do we approach '26? I mean, look, there's a lot of stuff we can't control. What we tried to do is be really clear-eyed about what we're seeing in the environment today. We didn't rely on anything necessarily changing except for the progression that we'll talk about from a category standpoint. We basically said the battery category is going to be down roughly 2% for the year. Trade policies are going to stay in place. Things that are macro factors, we basically took them as they are and rolled them forward. If you look at our EPS call, there is growth at the higher end of our range.
As we were contemplating it, we felt it was appropriate to build in some downside just so that we can absorb some shocks to the system, which we've seen over the last couple of years and not having to change our outlook. We were a little bit conservative in terms of the EPS growth. We didn't build in anything out of our control to cooperate over the year. I think we feel like it's an appropriate call, and one that we can achieve as we go through the year that's going to inevitably change along the way.
Peter Grom
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Got it. That makes a ton of sense. I'll pass it on. Thank you so much.
Jonathan Poldan
Vice President of Investor Relations and Treasurer, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Thanks, Peter.
Operator
Thank you. The next question comes from Lauren Lieberman at Barclays. Please go ahead.
Lauren Lieberman
Analyst, Barclays
Great, thanks so much. Good morning. Just wanted to take a step back maybe and a bigger picture look. Consumer slowdown, softening. Just wanted to get your perspective on maybe what's changed since we last spoke, both August and then you were at our conference. Sort of what's changed, what hasn't, and how are you thinking about the consumer and cost environment from here? Thanks.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Yeah. Lauren, I think if I start with gross margin, we saw the landscape changing. We had plans in place. I would say the gross margin projection largely as we expected. We knew Q4 was going to get hit by some of these transitory costs. We expected them to continue into 2026. They have, but we've also executed the plans to make them go away as we exit Q1. I would say the biggest changes we've just seen is softening consumer sentiment. You've heard it from a lot of our peers. You've certainly seen it in some of the macro data that as we progressed from August to September and into October, you really did see softening consumer sentiment. We're seeing it in the category data for batteries.
We are seeing some of the more recent time periods, some improvement in that, but we did not feel like it was appropriate to rely on that continuing to ramp up. Long term, we are still very bullish on the battery category. We expect it to be kind of a low single-digit grower, as we are going through a disruptive time. I think it is important to call that from a consumer standpoint, as we have. Gross margin, we have controlled what we can. Overall for the year, again, I just mentioned in Peter's question, down 2% is our call for value, but we are going to be able to offset that with some growth in other areas of our business.
Lauren Lieberman
Analyst, Barclays
Okay. Great. Just.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Oh, one other thing, Lauren. I'm sorry to cut you off on this. As we progress through the year, this is one thing I failed to mention. The category we're assuming is down 3% to 4% in the first quarter. As we progress, we are expecting stabilization in the category. We're going to start to lap some softer comps that you saw in 2025. I failed to mention that.
Lauren Lieberman
Analyst, Barclays
Okay. That's a big part of the driver of the sort of projected improvement in trends after Q1 or the comps.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Yes.
Lauren Lieberman
Analyst, Barclays
Okay. Okay. Great. All right. I'll pass it on. Thank you so much.
Jonathan Poldan
Vice President of Investor Relations and Treasurer, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Thanks, Lauren.
Operator
Thank you. The next question comes from Rob Ottenstein at Evercore. Please go ahead.
Robert Ottenstein
Analyst, Evercore
Great. Thank you very much. I was just wondering if you could talk a little bit about channel dynamics. Obviously, weaker consumer. How is the consumer responding in this environment in terms of which channels they are going to and shopping? What is going on at Amazon with you and the category? How are you responding to these different changes in consumer dynamics and shopping patterns? Thank you.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Good morning, Robert. Consumers are certainly seeking value. They're cautious. They're very comfortable shifting channels to be able to find the value of the product, and to meet their needs. That manifests itself in a lot of different ways. You've got brands, pack sizes, as you mentioned, channel. Certainly, e-commerce is a big part of that channel shifting that's going on. It's been a point of emphasis for us to make sure that we win in e-commerce. We had a really strong Q4 in e-commerce. We saw our e-commerce business grow more than 35% in Q4. We saw it grow 25% for the year. As we look ahead to 2026, we expect 15% growth off of that as we go into 2026. It's been an area we've invested in. It's an area where we're winning.
Over that time period, if I look in the aggregate over a 4, 13, and 52-week period, we're winning with consumers because Energizer is gaining share over each of those time periods. As consumers are seeking value, our broad portfolio of premium and value brands are there to meet consumers where they are, and we're capturing consumers.
Robert Ottenstein
Analyst, Evercore
Great, thank you very much.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Thanks, Robert.
Operator
Thank you. The next question comes from Andrea Teixeira at JPMorgan. Please go ahead.
Shovana Chowdhury
Equity Analyst, JPMorgan Chase & Co.
Hi. This is Shovana Chowdhury on for Andrea. Thanks for taking our question. On your management commentary, one of the levers to restore gross margin includes optimizing US manufacturing to maximize your future benefits from production credits. As such, can you give us a sense of magnitude of incremental benefit from your prior estimate of $35 to 40 million annually?
Jonathan Poldan
Vice President of Investor Relations and Treasurer, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Yeah, we are continuing to invest in domestic production to drive those credits. We think there could be upside of $15 to 20 million over what we've generated to date per year. That's where we'll continue to focus and try to recoup those.
Shovana Chowdhury
Equity Analyst, JPMorgan Chase & Co.
Thank you. Just to clarify, is that something that would be a benefit starting fiscal 2026 possibly, or is that more a fiscal 2027 onward story if you get this incremental benefit?
Jonathan Poldan
Vice President of Investor Relations and Treasurer, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Yeah, we anticipate that in 2026, kind of that level.
Shovana Chowdhury
Equity Analyst, JPMorgan Chase & Co.
Sounds good. Thanks. I'll pass it on.
Operator
Thank you. The next question comes from William Reuter at Bank of America. Please go ahead.
William? Reuter
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, Bank of America?Corporation
Hi. My first question on the weakness that you're seeing in consumers, do you expect that they're just reducing the amount of product that they have in their pantries, or do you believe that their behavior is changing such that they're utilizing devices that need batteries less? I'm just kind of trying to dig a little more into your expectation that the category is down by 2% or 3% or 4% this year, and then it bounces back in future years.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Consumers are changing. I mean, what we see is consumers will typically drain household inventory. Consumers will typically maybe skip a purchase cycle. You see that play out over a multiple quarter period. Everything stabilizes, and consumers go back to that historical low single-digit growth that we expect to see out of the category. We believe these are temporary behaviors out of consumers. It also manifests itself with channel shifting, with pack size changes, and other things that come through in the category data. We do expect a reversion back to more normalized behavior as we head into 2026.
William? Reuter
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, Bank of America?Corporation
Got it. Just a follow-up for me. I think that there had been an algorithm of an expectation of kind of half a turn of deleverage annually. If I look back over the last handful of years, leverage really hasn't moved a whole lot. I guess what is your expectation for that deleveraging path? In that context, how will you think about allocation relative to share repurchases, which you guys did $90 million this year?
Jonathan Poldan
Vice President of Investor Relations and Treasurer, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Yeah. Look, first priority is going to be to pay down debt. We think we can get back to resumption of normalized cash in 2025. We were down, and that was really largely due to our plastic-free packaging transition in North America. We invested in both inventories, so working capital was way up for the year. We invested in a lot of CapEx, frankly, to make that product. That should normalize both of those as we head into 2026. We think that we can get that kind of somewhere north of 10% on free cash flow. We would focus on paying down $150 to 200 million of debt. I think the offset from a leverage perspective will be where the earnings ends up. We'll have to see where that comes in, but it won't probably be all the way to half a turn.
It'd be something less than that if the earnings fall off. I will say that we generated decent cash as we finished up the fourth quarter, and we've paid down about $80 million of debt so far in the first quarter. We're making good progress, and we'll continue to push there.
William? Reuter
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, Bank of America?Corporation
Great. That's all for me. Thank you.
Jonathan Poldan
Vice President of Investor Relations and Treasurer, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, if you have any questions, please press star one. The next question comes from Brian McNamara at Canaccord Genuity. Please go ahead.
Brian? McNamara
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, Canaccord?Genuity Corp.
Good morning, guys. Thanks for taking the question. I'm curious how your retail partners are behaving as it relates to channel inventories. We've heard a variety of takes from other companies, but the predominance has generally been they've been pretty tight on inventories heading into the holiday season. I'm curious how your categories are being impacted by that.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Good question, Brian. I think that plays a part in kind of our Q4, Q1 dynamic that we were highlighting today. We saw displays go in at the end of Q4 that we thought were going to go in in Q1. Obviously, with some softening in the consumer sentiment in the category, you've seen lighter replenishment as we've gotten into Q1 simply because they're managing inventory more tightly. We've expected that for purposes of what the outlook we're providing, we're expecting that to continue for the balance of this year. I think we do expect tighter inventory management as we progress through 2026.
Brian? McNamara
Managing Director and Senior Analyst, Canaccord?Genuity Corp.
Great. My other question was already asked, so thanks. Appreciate it.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Thanks, Brian.
Operator
Thank you. We have no further questions. I will turn the call back over to Mark LaVigne for closing comments.
Mark LaVigne
President and CEO, Energizer Holdings, Inc.
Thanks, everyone, for joining today. Have a good rest of the day.
Operator
Ladies and gentlemen, this concludes your conference call for today. We thank you for participating, and we ask that you please disconnect your lines.

Operator
There won't be all that many surprises because we published our preliminary figures on 23 January. Today you'll be getting the full picture, and we'll be focusing on current topics such as the power plant strategy. Here with us in the room today, we have the CEO, Christian Bruch, and the CFO, Maria Ferraro. Christian Bruch will give you an overview of the past quarter, and then the CFO, Maria Ferraro, will give details on the Q1 figures. After that, as usual, both will be available to answer your questions. Mr. Bruch will be speaking in German, Ms. Ferraro in English. There'll be two webcasts, one for the original, where you will hear the original, and then the English line, where you will hear the English interpretation, and Ms. Ferraro will be transmitted in the original.
Following the QA, journalists will have a separate telephone number where they can sign up, and we sent you the link with the invitation for today's call. You can also sign up for this telephone dial-in today. If you are in the webcast and in the telephone line, then please put yourselves on mute in the telephone line so we don't have any feedback. The presentation can be downloaded on our homepage. Please remember there won't be a written speech today. Both will be speaking freely. I'd just like to remind you of our safe harbor statement on forward-looking statements, and this can be found on page two of our quarterly presentation. I'd like to hand over now to Christian Bruch, our CEO.
Christian Bruch
President and CEO, Siemens Energy AG
Thank you, Tim. Also, good morning. As Tim already said, the surprise today was certainly not too big. We already published our figures on 23 January. The reason for this was, as you know, that there were shifts between the quarters. This is a project-based business with a certain volatility and in an extremely dynamic market environment in energy. It's not always easy to plan specifically according to quarters, and we decided to early on inform the market about the good Q1. We have to say this, we had a very good start, good beginning of the year across all of the segments, particularly Gas Services, Grid Technologies, and Transformation of Industry that stand out with very, very good order intakes.
We have a record order intake of EUR 15.4 billion, and we assume that H1 will be stronger than H2. At the end of the day, you see that energy is a good and dynamic business segment and is growing considerably. Revenue amounted to EUR 7.6 billion. All segments contributed, very strong increase in Grid Technologies due to the strong order intake that we had in 2023, and Maria will, as usual, go into more detail with the figures. The profit before special items increased considerably to EUR 208 million. In Q1 of last year, it was EUR -282 million. This is a positive development as well.
As expected in Q1, we also had special items of EUR 1.6 billion that we were able to record. This is due to the sale of the 18% stake in Siemens Limited in India. Siemens Energy's earnings in Q1 amounted to around EUR 1.9 billion. Overall, I can say we're on track to achieve our targets for the year as a whole. We're working through the individual topics quarter by quarter. We have opportunities in the energy business and try to translate that into profitable growth. The other topic that we will continue to focus on are the quality problems or the solutions to the quality problems at Siemens Gamesa and at the same time, ramping up the production in the offshore business.
We know that we need to reestablish some of the confidence in the market. We're all working on this, step-by-step, and every quarter, we want to give you the opportunity to see what we are doing, what's happening. I'd like to say that working through all of these issues takes time. We want to do this with conscientiousness and diligence. I understand that there are questions how fast, how quick, how concrete, and whether we can be more precise. We try to balance this, and we're doing this step-by-step. Please understand that the technical studies have mostly been concluded. What does that mean?
Well, it means that the problems are being understood, and now what has been considered so far continues to be right. We continue to believe that they're right. Let me just put it into context again. You know that the provisions will be spent over the course of the next years. The biggest cash out is planned for 2025, but it all depends on the plans. As far as the offshore business is concerned, it's about ramping up the production, guaranteeing the ramp up of the production and working through the order backlog. Last year, we said that there were challenges in three areas. First, the disruption of the supply chain.
Secondly, the overly optimistic planning of the ramping up of the factories with the simultaneous introduction of new models, technologies, longer blades, and bigger cabins. That is something where we needed to try a few things before we can increase productivity. The third was the capacity expansion of the individual plants. Now we have achieved a lot regarding the supply chains. They've become more resilient. We've introduced more suppliers, additional suppliers. We've also bundled our procurement volumes in a more long-term way to cover the plans. When you look at the cash flow of Siemens Gamesa, you see that we've built up a little bit of stock. This is related to the offshore order backlog. We are addressing the issues from a construction point of view.
We've increased the capacities for the plants and have almost completed this. There are still individual aspects that need to be terminated, but now it is about step-by-step improving the processes in manufacturing. We need to focus on this, and as I said, this is a gradual process. The big ramp up is expected to take place in Q2 of the year. We're now introducing the new models, and the teams now need to be trained and improved, and the processes need to be improved. All we can say is it is happening step-by-step, and that's what we're focusing on. The next big issue last year was the counter guarantees from the federal government, the bank consortium, and the counter guarantees with the federal government have been signed now.
The agreement on EUR 11 billion that were signed by commercial banks based on the counter guarantee of the federal government has already entered into force. We do have the government guaranteeing EUR 7.5 billion as a counter guarantee. In addition to this, there will be an additional EUR 1 billion that has been guaranteed from three commercial banks. I always like to stress this because I'm being asked this repeatedly. It is a counter guarantee. It is a tool that is used for performance and payment measures. It is not a direct support, a direct subsidy from the state. We're paying a lot of fees to the state for this counter guarantee. I'd like to say this repeatedly because there is a big misunderstanding when it comes to that.
At the same time, we concluded the sale of the 18% share of Siemens Limited in India. I've already mentioned this, and I'd like to say thank you very much explicitly to Siemens AG for the fast and easy cooperation. These structures are anything but easy. It was difficult to do this, and it was great help for us that Siemens AG focused on this. We already announced this last year. We are progressing with regard to the focusing of the core business of Siemens Gamesa. One aspect of this is the sale of a 32% participation in the company Windar Renovables. This is a company that predominantly builds towers for wind mills. This is not a focus of us. The sale has been sold now.
The sale has been completed, but we continue to work with Windar, and we're also working on the integration of the central functions between Siemens Gamesa and Siemens Energy, as it was originally stipulated in the merger. We are working on achieving the originally communicated synergy goals. I'd like to mention a couple of examples. What I'm happy about when it comes to this is that we have not had any problems finding good examples in none of the quarters. That's always a positive sign. It shows that the energy market is both very, very dynamic and also that we have a good portfolio. Let me pick out two examples. One is our power plant project in Kazakhstan.
This is another project where old coal-fired power plants are being replaced by gas turbine power plants and cogeneration plants in the Kazakh capital of Almaty. You know that until 2030, Kazakhstan wants to reduce its greenhouse emissions by 25%. Coal continues to be an important fossil fuel in Kazakhstan, so such a project plays an important role in addition to other energy projects that are being discussed in Kazakhstan. Second example is from the strongly growing business unit, Grid Technologies, Viking Link. It's an HVDC link, high voltage direct current connection between the United Kingdom and Denmark. It's an almost 800km long underwater cable to ensure the exchange of power and ensure that there is guaranteed power for 2.5 million households.
This is an example for the projects that we can see everywhere in the order intake of Grid Technologies now. The nice thing about this project is that it was taken into operation three years after the work started. This shows that projects can be concluded quickly in the grid sector, and this is necessary for the energy transformation. One more thing I'd like to mention before I give the floor to Maria. It's the general market environment. At the Capital Market Day in November, we already said the market environment continues to be good. We do, with a certain level of concern, look at the Suez Canal geopolitical conflicts. In general, energy is an issue that currently sees an immense signal upswing. We see a positive demand at the global level.
At COP28 in Dubai, the discussions also stated that despite the good progress, the expansion, the speed of the expansion in the grid, particularly when it comes to renewable is not enough. There were declarations in Dubai focusing on tripling the capacity for renewable energies at the global level and doubling energy efficiency. Today, when it comes to the expansion until 2030, we are in a corridor where we can achieve 2.5, an increase of 2.5, when it comes to capacity. We're on the right track, but it needs to improve. You need to see that the big share of the expansion is taking place in China. China is ahead. Other regions in the world are slightly lagging behind. We'll now have to see that the expansion gets the necessary speed it needs.
If we look at wind power in Germany, we've made a lot of strides forward, but we haven't yet reached the speed necessary in order to achieve our goals at the end of the day. I think it is positive that we now have some basic pillars in the power plant strategy that were communicated, for example, that there will be a capacity market, among other things, that before the capacity market is introduced, there will have to be tenders for natural gas power plants that can then be switched to hydrogen. The third thing I think is positive is that hydrogen and promoting hydrogen has been removed from the back burner again. This is an impulse that is needed. That's the right analysis.
Now it's about putting the details into practice. How is it financed from the side of the government? How does it look like in concrete terms in 2024? We really have to go into the tenders. The global market is very tight as far as demand is concerned, so it's important to get moving here. This was a first important step. Now I'd like to give the floor to Maria for the figures.
Maria Ferraro
CFO, Siemens Energy AG
Thank you, Christian. Good morning, everyone. A warm welcome also from my side. Thank you for joining us today. Let me get right into our financial performance in Q1. Of course, as Christian mentioned, you already saw our preliminary numbers, which we published on 23 January. Today, I want to give you some more insights, perhaps starting with our performance at the group level. We did have a solid start to the year, and we continue to see positive momentum across all our former GP businesses. Siemens Gamesa performed within our expectations in Q1. Our order development was outstanding, better than expected, reflecting the continuous favorable demand pattern that we see in our markets. We also did benefit from some pull-forward effects in certain businesses. Looking at growth, it stands at 24% comparable despite a high basis of comparison.
This has resulted in orders for this quarter of EUR 15.4 billion. This is the highest ever order intake in a quarter to date. The book-to-bill ratio is very strong at slightly above two. This again is driving growth in our order backlog to a new high of EUR 108 billion. Revenue also grew significantly with almost 13% increase on a comparable basis. What's important is all segments contributed to this growth. The biggest contribution is coming from our Grid Technologies business. Service revenue also had a very strong start to the year and helped us here. This grew slightly more than the new unit business, and it is important also that we had a very strong service season across all business areas. Profit before special items did improve to EUR 208 million.
All of our business areas either improved or stayed at prior year's level. Our profit margin before special items came in at 2.7%. Special items, as already mentioned, included the pre-tax gain from the sale of our 18% stake in Siemens Limited India, as already indicated to you, of around EUR 1.7 billion, which brings us to the profit for the quarter of EUR 1.9 billion and a net income of EUR 1.6 billion. Free cash flow pre-tax came in at EUR -283 million. This is a bit of a mixed picture where we had positive contributions from our former GP businesses, supported by the higher profitability as well as, of course, with a high order intake value. You also get advanced payments from our customers.
This was offset by the negative free cash flow as expected at Siemens Gamesa of EUR -1.2 billion. At Siemens Gamesa, as I just mentioned, it's very important to note that this is seasonal in nature. The high cash outflow was, of course, expected and is as a result of the losses and seasonality as mentioned, where we're building up operating net working capital to of course ensure that we're able to convert our backlog in that business and the ramp up, of course, in our offshore business. Now, just maybe perfect segue into the next slide, looking at our order backlog. Of course, what's important here as always is that our order backlog really does provide us with visibility on revenue and conversion well beyond a 12-month timeframe.
In Q1, the backlog continued to grow, as mentioned, to a new record high of EUR 118 billion. We mentioned this at the capital market day in November, where we provided new midterm targets for all our business areas. The margins, this is what's important. The margins that we see in our order backlog are supporting these targets, and we continue to see a positive progression also in Q1 within our backlog. What's also important is close to 50% of the backlog is service business, and this of course provides us with excellent visibility for future recurring resilient revenue with high margins and of course good cash conversion.
We're also seeing strong growth in our new units business, and this is also important, of course, as we continue to grow our installed base and new units help us create additional service revenue in the future. Again, the backlog is important and it's excellent that it's growing, but we need to continue to convert that into profitable revenue over the years to come. Looking at the next page, our liquidity, our return to a net cash position. As you know, we proactively initiated measures to strengthen our balance sheet with significant near-term cash measures, targeting EUR 2.5 to 3 billion cash inflows by means of the acceleration of our existing divestment program and including the sale of the 18% stake in Siemens Limited India to Siemens AG.
Just to repeat, we closed the sale of the 18% stake in Siemens Limited India to Siemens AG early December. This resulted in a cash inflow of roughly EUR 2.1 billion in cash and a one-time P&L gain of close to EUR 1.7 billion. Again, you notice the difference between the profit gain here and the cash inflow from the transaction. This is due to the existing book value we had for the Siemens Limited India share investment. The profit booked in special items represents the gain made on that value. Overall, all things considered, our liquidity position remains strong. Our cash and cash equivalents at the end of the quarter grew to EUR 5.3 billion, while our financial debt shrank to EUR 3.9 billion, of which 3.2 therein is long-term in nature.
As a result, we returned to an adjusted net cash position of approximately EUR 840 million. This again is in line with our focus to maintain a strong balance sheet, which of course is underlying our commitment to maintaining an investment-grade rating. Now let's take a look at the business areas and start with Gas Services. Q1 was a very solid start for Gas Services. Orders exceeded last year's high level by 13.1%. This again driven by higher volume of large orders and the backlog then grew for GS to EUR 42 billion. Revenue grew by just shy of 11% on a comparable basis to EUR 2.7 billion, again against a very high prior year level.
Looking back, as I said earlier, with respect to the strong service performance, we had a favorable mix in business this quarter with both service and new unit business increasing here. Profit before special items came in very close to the strong level of last year's quarter at EUR 313 million or 11.7%. Moving to Grid Technologies, which also had a very strong start into the fiscal year. Here you see an outstanding order development that continues with the overall positive market environment for Grid Technologies. Orders in Q1 exceeded already the high level from prior year by just shy of 33% and rose to EUR 8.2 billion. This development was driven by GT's product business and HVDC orders in Germany, also in part benefiting from pull-forward effects.
The book-to-bill was just shy of four, and the backlog rose to EUR 28 billion. Revenue also grew substantially by just over 33% and came in at EUR 2.1 billion. This again, supported by the strong order intake conversion that we saw in previous years. Profit before special items came in strong at EUR 213 million. This is a 10.2% and significant improvement versus last year. Partly due again to our higher revenue, but also thanks to the higher margin in the process order backlog. Now let's turn to Transformation of Industry on the next page. Here, the focus on selectivity with improved price risk profiles and continued focus, which is key on executing with operational excellence and a focus on productivity. This is all nicely reflected in the Q1 results for Transformation of Industry.
Here we booked EUR 1.6 billion in orders in Q1. This is a 39% increase comparable to last year. The book-to-bill came in at 1.4, just over 1.4, and the backlog rose to EUR 7 billion. Revenue also grew significantly by just shy of 18% on a comparable basis, with all four independently managed businesses showing double-digit growth. Service also a contributing factor here, and we had a strong customer demand for year-end services. Profit nearly doubled to EUR 105 million with a corresponding margin of just over 9%.
This was driven by higher revenue, as just mentioned, but also by better pricing, and was also here, and we talked about that, we had some timing in shifts and project shifts, and here you saw that was particularly influenced by timing in products and projects, currency impacts, and as mentioned, quite a strong service start. Now moving on to our wind business, Siemens Gamesa. Looking at orders in Q1, this was slightly above prior level. In the onshore business, as you know and as fully expected, our orders were slightly halved due to the temporary suspension of sales activities for the 4.X and 5.X onshore turbines. However, this was made up by the strong growth in service orders and in offshore.
Revenue grew at just shy of 5% comparable, though we saw again the decline in onshore due to the known issues as just mentioned, and the offshore ramp up challenges. This was more than made up by the increase in service. As I mentioned earlier, we had a strong service Q1, and this was across all businesses. Profit before special items came in at EUR -426 million. Last year's quarter was at EUR -472 million. If you recall, there were charges related to quality issues in prior year quarter. With that, let me summarize the quarter very briefly. We had a solid start to the fiscal year. We're on track to meet our full year targets. Again, Q1 is encouraging and also benefit from some timing and project shifts.
This is completely normal in our business, especially with the market dynamics that we're seeing. This is why we maintain our guidance. We're also making strong progress, as mentioned in our ongoing disposal program of non-core assets, and therefore are very confident to reach the upper end of the EUR 2.5 billion to 3 billion full year target for cash proceeds. Our goal overall to have an adjusted net cash position at the end of fiscal year 2024. On the next page, let's look at our outlook for fiscal year 2024, which remains unchanged. We continue to expect Siemens Energy comparable revenue growth in the range of 3% to 7%. Profit margin before special items between -2% and +1%.
For the fiscal year 2024, our assumptions on growth per business area remains unchanged, as well as the negative profit before special items of -EUR 2 billion that we expect for Siemens Gamesa. For the group, we expect a net income up to EUR 1 billion, including impacts from disposals, and we continue to assume a negative free cash flow pre-tax of around -EUR 1 billion, again, not including proceeds from the disposals. With that concludes my part of the presentation, and I hand back to you, Christian. Thank you.
Christian Bruch
President and CEO, Siemens Energy AG
Thank you very much, Maria. Let me conclude by addressing a topic that I think has been on the minds of many people in Germany over the past few months. The speed with which right-wing populist parties are gaining support all over Europe, and the question of what a society we want to have. Let me just stress first, the challenges that we're all dealing with nowadays are tremendous, but there are no easy solution, even though some claim that it's about explaining complex solutions in a better way to really show possible ways, out. This requires effort, money, and consideration for each other. I'd like to state that as a company, we depend on having an open, transparent, diverse society. We have 97,000 people working for us, people from more than 130 nationalities.
In Germany, we have 26,000 employees from all different nations. That's 27% of our entire workforce. We only generate 8% of our revenue in Germany. This international character creates jobs and wealth for us and is of essential importance for us as a company. We want to maintain it here, and I'm very proud of an international board. I depend on everybody feeling welcome and at ease here in the country. For the company, I'd like to highlight that, and reiterate it. Everything else would be detrimental to the success of the business of the company and the wealth and affluence of the country. If we want to focus on making this company a successful one, we need an open, transparent society that is also diverse. Thank you very much. With this, Tim, we're moving on to the questions.
Operator
Thank you very much, Christian and Maria. Journalists, you now have the opportunity to ask questions. Now the technical information. Once again, you can ask questions in person if you've dialed into the telephone line. We sent you the login data with the invitation, and if you want to ask a question, please press asterisk and one on your keyboard. Otherwise, you can ask questions in the chat if you like, in the webcast. You're familiar with the technical details. To make sure we don't have any feedback, please terminate your webcast, unless of course you only speak English, then of course you can listen to the English interpretation. You can ask your questions in English or German, and it will be answered in the same language.
Asterisk and one if you want to ask a question. Now I think we can take the first question. This is Mr. Hübner from the Handelsblatt. Go ahead, sir.
Axel Hübner
Journalist, Handelsblatt
I have two questions. What about the sales and revenue potential in Kazakhstan, I believe? What is the capacity that you have there? The second question, the cost for the counter guarantees. When will we see them in the quarterly reports? Where and what will the amounts be?
Markus Frühauf
Editor, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung
Good morning, Mr. Hübner. Well, the counter guarantees, that's something Maria will take. As far as the CapEx strategy, I would like to mention two topics that are in the foreground. Gas turbines themselves and then the pilot projects for hydrogen. In other words, to have a demonstration of 100% hydrogen turbines. We'll have to see how quickly these all arrive. You talked about 2.5 GW. You've seen that.
Christian Bruch
President and CEO, Siemens Energy AG
This is something that we want to participate in this, at least, I would say, to have a market share that we have in this turbine area. We can assume that we will have some of these projects. We hope we will be awarded these contracts. This would then mean jobs in Berlin. I would say that on this basis, we have to see that we can get this as quickly as possible when it comes to the tenders. The whole market, this relates to us and our competitors there, it's a very tight market. Of course, we will be involved in these tenders for our customers. Of course, we would be interested in having a large share of this. Maria, go ahead.
Maria Ferraro
CFO, Siemens Energy AG
Hello, Axel. Good morning. Thank you for the question regarding the guarantee and the fees. The fees, of course, depend on the term and the volume that's actually utilized of the facility. Therefore, in terms of, we're not able to precisely quantify that at this point in time. However, maybe I can shed some light a little bit on the construct. We have a fee, of course, for the guarantees that are payable to banks. That's a normal standard market fee. Then on top of that, we have to pay the additional fee to the federal government for the counter guarantee. The total costs are above, let's say, what we have paid in the past. In that additional part we have estimated is included in our guidance at this point in time, based again on an estimate.
Operator
Thank you very much. The strategy, Michael Watzka also has a question from Deutschlandfunk. I think that question has already been answered. The next question would then be Christoph Steitz from Reuters.
Christoph Steitz
Chief Company News Correspondent, Reuters
Good morning from Frankfurt. I have three questions. Do you plan to adjust capacities in onshore? You said that you will be reviewing the portfolio, so maybe there will be fewer products or fewer markets. How will this be reflected in the production sites? My second question, what about claims for damages? You mentioned that some of the components had problems. Can you give us any information? Maybe you could give us an update there. Then a question on the structure. Mr. Bruch, Siemens Energy is involved in many areas of the energy transformation. Maybe it's too much, and this is maybe the company.
Well, we need to ask the question as to maybe a leaner positioning might be better, and then some parts are going very well and other parts of the company are not doing well at all. I'd like to have your reaction on that. Thank you very much.
Christian Bruch
President and CEO, Siemens Energy AG
Thank you for those questions. With regard to capacity adjustments, of course, you can see this in the orders. The capacity utilization is something that we also have to reflect there as well. In the past, we've seen that we had activities where we had plants in Brazil, for instance, that these were shut down. This is not something that was really in the headlines. We continue to observe all of this to make sure that any lower capacity utilization, which we have as a result of not offering the onshore products, that this is also something that can be reflected in the structural costs. This is work in progress right now, but as I said, we try to strike a balance here so that we also don't want to lose the opportunities that are out there. We are working on this step-by-step.
When we have taken a decision, of course we will announce that to you. As I said, as in other areas as well, we assume that this is much more evolutionary and not revolutionary. Things are being done step-by-step. When it comes to claims for damages, yes, things are running there. There are some suppliers where we believe that we can claim damages. Of course, this is something that is going to keep this generic in my explanations. I could say that we have also some challenges that we have in order to give you some amounts here. The smallest amount of the quality problems are spare parts. The supplier will have to be ready for that. But the more expensive costs are cranes and perhaps, payments for delays. But these are things that we are paying attention to and we hope to get contributions there.
The structure of the company. Well, let me put it this way. This is something that every CEO has to be concerned with. They always have to take a look at the structure and say, "Okay, let's take a look at the portfolio. Does it all fit? Does it make sense what we have? I still believe that we have to remember one thing. We have problems with wind. It's not a structural problem, and we saw that as well if you take a look at the share price, let's say in 2023 between the 1st and the 10th, and then you can see this before we communicated the quality cost, we had a wonderful share price development, and this is something that was then damaged as a result of the problems with wind.
Of course, it's a question here of saying, will we be able to get the right focus, and will we have the right approach? I do think that at this point in time, I don't think that we. Well, it's one thing we should not forget. When we began, people would love to have seen us exit from grids and gas. Look at where we stand today. Those are things that you have to weigh, the pros and the cons. I think right now that renewables maybe are seen in too negative a light in some areas, and that is why it's a very complex picture. We'll have to wait and see, and we'll have to see that we're facing up to the criticisms, and we'll look and see, is this a good structure that we have which we can manage?
As I said, at this point in time, I think that the main issue is to solve the problems with wind, and that's it.
Operator
Michael Flemming with Börsen-Zeitung. Good morning.
Michael Flemming
Correspondent, Börsen-Zeitung
Good morning, Mr. Bruch, Ms. Ferraro. I have two questions. You mentioned the surprisingly good result in Q1 and said that this is due to project shifts. Does that have an impact on Q2? Will that be slightly weaker because some of the projects were shifted into Q1, or will there not be an impact? Second question, you mentioned the record high order intake and the order backlog with Grid Technologies EUR 28 billion. You mentioned that, Ms. Ferraro. With EUR 8 to 9 billion annual revenue, this is a lot.Will there be a capacity expansion?
Maria Ferraro
CFO, Siemens Energy AG
Let me put my speaker on. That would help. Hello, Herr Flemming. Good morning, and thank you for the questions. I think with respect to the timing, topics and how that worked in Q1, let me try to shed a bit of light. Again, this is normal for us. Number one. Number two is, generally speaking, our Q1 is seasonally stronger. This is also something that you see, of course, as mentioned with the service business, etc. Underlying, this is something that we've worked hard on in the last years, underlying the operational performance is progressing well. I think just to lay the basis. With respect to the project shifts and timings, let me talk about revenue, for example first.
Here, as mentioned, I said there was a strong service season in certain areas, better than expected factory output, of course, because you see that we have that momentum continuing, and therefore there was some shifts with respect to revenue recognition and of course then the related profit recognition. This is to a certain extent pull-forwarded amounts, let's say, that again will not be in the remaining three quarters, but this is to an extent compensated for. This is the same and true for profits. Here, again, the pull-forward revenue is creating additional profits, but we also benefited things like from hedging effects. This will unwind. This was a mid-double-digit amount and a couple of other operational contractual topics. Again, contractual changes, etc. Very normal for our business.
This is something we see all the time, except in this particular quarter it was particularly positive. I hope that sheds some light. We know that we have some seasonality. We know that it was a very strong Q1, but again, this is all of the hard work on top of the underlying operating performance that continues to pay off.
Christian Bruch
President and CEO, Siemens Energy AG
Good morning, Mr. Flemming. Thank you for the question. The answer is twofold. With the capacity expansion in Grid, there are two aspects. One is people. For two years, we have been carrying out a dedicated program on setting up workforce in different regions in the world for Grid. Second is the expansion of factory plant expansions. We set this at the Capital Markets Day, two sites that will be realized, and I think over the course of the year, we can provide you with more details on that. We're in the process of doing this, and that helps us to get rid of the order backlog.
Operator
Next, a question from the chat, Manu Álvarez with El Correo. Similar to Pilar Blázquez, asked a question about the guarantee negotiations with the Spanish government.
Christian Bruch
President and CEO, Siemens Energy AG
Yes, they're on their way. I'm grateful for the support of the Spanish government in close cooperation with the Spanish banks. Again, this is work in progress, but we do see positive support from the Spanish government. Pedro Sánchez, I think, said that in an interview at the World Economic Forum, that the Spanish government is willing to support industry in general, and wind industry in Spain, and I'm grateful for that, but we're still sorting out the details.
Markus Frühauf
Editor, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung
Manu Álvarez had two more questions. The first, what about the sales process of the eight plants in Spain? What happened with that?
Christian Bruch
President and CEO, Siemens Energy AG
Mr. Álvarez, we're not going to say anything about this because we've never done that. That was a speculation in the media. We're not going to pick that up today.
The second question referred to the sale of 4.X and 5.X turbines. That you don't have a scheduled date to start production and sales of the 4.X and 5.X turbine again. Could Siemens Gamesa need the entire year, or they could live without the entire year 2024 without starting production of the design? Could it be that we will not be selling them this year? Well, this is first of all the question when will we start selling them and when will the work also be in the plants? There will be a delay, but we do have a backlog that we have to execute.
We have some obligations there, and of course there is some work to be done. We have that as well, and you can see that in our orders. As I said, in other turbines and as well, in onshore, we've taken in some orders, not that many for 5.X. That's why I would say that once we can say we're going to begin this, then we will inform the market, but not beforehand. I really want to make sure that we've worked through everything, ticked everything off. We can ask you to be a bit patient on this point, please.
Operator
The next question is from the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung. Mr. Frühauf, go ahead.
Markus Frühauf
Editor, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung
Good morning, Mr. Bruch, Ms. Ferraro. I didn't quite understand 2.5 from this disposal of Siemens Limited. I didn't quite understand the cash in and the cash flow on this point. You maybe could tell us how this will develop in the future as well. Is this something that you will continue on?
Christian Bruch
President and CEO, Siemens Energy AG
I'm sorry the sound is very poor. The sound quality was not good. I'm going to mute you just for a second. The sound was poor, and I understood that we have this disposal and the question of cash flow. He didn't understand the cash flow with the Siemens India.
Markus Frühauf
Editor, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung
I didn't understand the second question. I didn't understand it, says Mr. Bruch.
Christian Bruch
President and CEO, Siemens Energy AG
You didn't understand the question. Okay. The Gamesa cash flow. Maybe she can take that.
Maria Ferraro
CFO, Siemens Energy AG
Maybe add some clarity because, when it comes to disposals, this was a sale, if you'd like, of our Siemens Limited stake, 18%. It had a disposal value, so cash in of EUR 2.1 billion. However, this is not in the definition of operating cash flow. Therefore you only see it, if you'd like, in our profit ultimately and therefore in our net income on our P&L, excuse me. That forms part of what we're talking in the guidance that we've given for net cash from disposals, where we see by the end of this fiscal year, EUR 2.5 to 3 billion of net proceeds from disposals. Hopefully that clarifies. Then, of course, the P&L impact, there was an investment value attached to the Siemens Limited.
That's why, although the proceeds were EUR 2.1 billion, the impact on our net income was EUR 1.7 billion. Hopefully that has clarified your question. It's one-time in nature. I think you asked a forward-looking question on that cash flow. It's one-time in nature and the transaction closed in December within our Q1.
Operator
I see that he lost the connection, so it seems he had poor reception, but I'll talk to him on the phone later on. The next question is Mr. Viktor Ecle-Dörner from Bloomberg. Good morning, Mr. Eckle-Dörner.
Viktor Ecle-Dörner
Reporter, Bloomberg
Good morning to everyone. I have two quick questions. How detailed is the repair plan for the defective turbines? Maybe you could give us more precise information. Will there be short-term measures that we consider? How much of these would be long-term, and how is it going to take? I also wanted to ask something about the turbines. Are you going to order them? In other words, the orders, are you going to be delivering them, or have you stopped delivery there as well? What about the 4.X and 5.X turbines? These have not been restarted again, but will you be taking on new orders for the 4.X and 5.X turbines? Have you suspended everything now? The question is, when do you plan to then start selling again for these turbines? Those are the questions that I have. Thank you.
Christian Bruch
President and CEO, Siemens Energy AG
Thank you. Let me just explain this. How detailed was it? Yes, it was detailed, very detailed, with support from external experts. When you have defined an external solution, someone from the outside has a look at it. We have a technical solution where we can see we have an engineering document, we've got the analysis, we've got the new calculations, the specifications for the new component. Then it goes into a procurement or manufacturing process. We're going to take a look for the suppliers, new bearings, new different places, whatever.
It depends on the delivery times for the components. It could take some time, and that is why we assume that, and you can see this in the cash flow that we announced at the Capital Market Day, that most of the activities will begin in 2025 and then will be executed over the following years. When cash is spent for the components, we buy the components and we commission things, that doesn't mean that we will have all the turbines installed or repaired by that. At the same time, we continuously work on turbines and we carry out minor upgrades. That's due to the fact that for most of our turbines, we have a service contract.
What we're trying to do is that in this course of normal service work, we try to take care of minor upgrades at the same time. Now the timeline. The question is, do we need a crane or not? That is a lot of effort involved there, and that's something that we can also determine the cost. That's the planning that we're doing right now. When will I do what and where? Once that has been concluded, we will be able to say, "Okay, this is how it'll be distributed." Let's assume that the main amount of our activities will be in 2025 and thereafter. That is why, as I said, the turbines are running. We don't have the availability we would like to have for the turbines, but this is something that is a step-by-step process.
To clarify things, we are not accepting orders for 4.X and 5.X. We've stopped selling them for the time being. Over the course of 2024, we will then decide when we might be able to do so. We can't tell you that exactly right now, but we're working and executing the older, given orders and handing them over to the customers. This continues to go on because we need to deliver from our backlog, and that is why this is running as normal as possible. Thank you.
Thank you. We don't have any further questions, not on the phone lines nor in the chat, so we're ending today's telephone conference. Thank you very much for participating. Thank you very much for your interest. If you have more questions, follow-up questions, the press team and I are available. I've just seen that Mr. Frühauf is back online, but we'll call you back because your connection was very bad. The telephone conference with the analysts will start at 11:30. Reason for this is, Vestas is also presenting its figures today, and many analysts cover both companies, so our PR department provided the special service of pushing our analyst call slightly back. You can call in but not ask questions. The link is on our website. Next official date is 26 February, our virtual AGM.
We have a special service for everybody who's interested. You can listen to the general debate on the live stream. Thank you very much. Stay healthy. See you soon.
